sentences.text: Revenue compounded 6.6% a year from $37.8 billion in FY2017 to $67.4 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F196].
The path was flat through FY2022, then two step changes: 17.7% growth in FY2023 and 17.3% in FY2026 [D280][D421].
The FY2023 step came from the Cerner acquisition, which contributed $5.9 billion of revenue, 11.8% of the year [S61][D604][P48].
FY2026 growth came from cloud, as cloud applications and cloud infrastructure contributed 16% and 84% of cloud revenue growth [P17].
Cloud Infrastructure is now the growth engine: $18.1 billion, 26.9% of revenue, up 76.9% and adding 13.7pp [S92][D643][D644][D645].
Cloud Applications added 2.8pp on 11.3% growth, while Software License fell 8.9% and subtracted 0.8pp [D668][D667][D682][D681].
The Americas contributed 14.2pp of the 17.3% growth and now are 66.0% of revenue [D470][D421][D468].
Operating income grew 16.6% against 17.3% revenue growth, an incremental margin of 29.4% [D422][D421][D442].
Diluted EPS grew 34.3% against 36.5% net income growth, with the diluted share count up 1.7% [D425][D423][D438].
Operating margin was 30.6% in FY2026, below the 32.2% window median and far below the 37.6% FY2021 high [F34][D788][D787].
It slipped 0.2pp as operating costs grew 17.7% against 17.3% revenue growth [D433][D436][D421].
The drag was infrastructure expense for cloud growth, which lifted cloud and software expenses by $6.0 billion and cut that segment's margin to 58.9% [P19][D761].
R&D fell to 15.3% of revenue, the window low, adding 1.9pp, as growth slowed to 4.2% on higher employee and equipment costs [D399][D795][D444][D435][P12].
Net margin rose 3.5pp to 25.2% as the effective tax rate fell to 28.4% from 39.2%, helped by $1.5 billion more stock-based compensation tax benefit [D434][F54][D407][D360][P9].
Operating cash flow rose 53.6% to $32.0 billion, 47.5% of revenue, but capex of $55.7 billion pushed free cash flow to -$23.7 billion [D426][F84][D406][F94][F104].
The $34.4 billion capex increase was the main investing outflow, partly offset by $4.3 billion from the Ampere sale [P5].
Operating cash flow gained on higher net income and $4.6 billion of customer prepayments with a significant financing component [P6].
Free cash flow was -1.39x net income against a 1.06x window median, and capex ran 7.30x D&A [D409][D800][D410].
Net debt widened to $97.6 billion, 145.0% of revenue, the 0th percentile against six software peers whose median net cash is -0.5% of revenue [D414][D415][D815][D816].
Debt rose 39.9% to $129.5 billion on $42.7 billion of senior notes and $5.0 billion of mandatory convertible preferred [D440][D413][P7].
Buybacks plus dividends were only $5.9 billion, with repurchases down to $95 million [D416][X155].
The diluted share count rose 1.7%, reversing the 11.9% annual shrink of FY2019 [D438][D114].
Cash and investments of $31.9 billion cover only 1.3 years of the latest burn, and $260 billion of data-center lease commitments sit off balance sheet [D419][D412][P1].
Free cash flow has run below net income for two years, at -0.03x in FY2025 and -1.39x in FY2026 [D362][D409].
Net cash has fallen into deeper net debt for two straight years, from -$76.2 billion to -$97.6 billion [D320][D367][D414].
FY2026 net income in the table is proxy-sourced and rounded; the 10-K figure is $17.1 billion [F44][X20].
Free cash flow margin: a return above the 26.0% window median would confirm the capex cycle is peaking; another year near the -35.2% low would not [D794][D792].
Operating margin: holding above the 30.6% latest level would show cloud infrastructure leverage; a drop toward the 25.7% FY2022 low would reverse it [F34][D786].
Net cash: any narrowing of the -$97.6 billion gap would ease balance-sheet strain; further widening would extend it [D414].
